name: veterinary_clinic_system_047_exam_room_turnover_report
instruction: Produce an exam-room turnover report, batched under the episode batch code, by joining appointments, locations, and providers. For every (location_id, room) pair that has at least one appointment in the trailing 30 days or the next 14 days, create one ops_reports row with report='room_turnover', batch_code, location_id, room, location_name (from locations), completed_last_30 = count of appointments with status 'completed' and dp(appointment_date) in [ep-30, ep), booked_next_14 = count of appointments with status in ('scheduled','confirmed') and dp(appointment_date) in [ep, ep+14), turnover_score = completed_last_30 + booked_next_14, distinct_patients = distinct patient_id count across both windows, distinct_providers = distinct provider_id count across both windows, primary_provider_id = the provider_id with the most appointments in that (location, room) across both windows (tie -> lowest numeric provider id). Then create one ops_reports row with report='room_turnover_summary', batch_code, total_turnover = sum of turnover_score, busiest_pair = '<location_id>/<room>' with the highest turnover_score (tie -> lexicographically smallest), all_pairs = sorted list of '<location_id>/<room>' strings, and avg_turnover = round(total_turnover / len(all_pairs), 1) if any pairs, else 0.0. The past window is half-open [ep-30, ep); the future window is half-open [ep, ep+14). Only appointments with status 'completed' count in the past bucket; only 'scheduled' or 'confirmed' count in the future bucket. Delete any existing room_turnover / room_turnover_summary rows for this batch before writing.
_steps_note: par_steps and max_steps must be measured against a live container in the QC session; do not set final values without a real gold run.

success_criteria.summary: Exactly one room_turnover row per (location, room) pair with all derived fields matching live data, plus one room_turnover_summary row. Counts, distincts, primary provider, busiest pair, and average are computed independently by raw-row Python and SQL and must agree. All other collections canary-checked.

checks.expect: exact per-pair metrics and summary, keyed by batch_code and report
every aggregate in each room_turnover row is computed both by raw-row Python and independent SQL; the two agree and match what was written

hazards: Room name collision across locations: 'Exam 1' exists at all three locations. Snapshot rows id 4 (Exam 1, location 1, checked_in), id 5 (Exam 1, location 2, checked_in), and id 6 (Exam 1, location 3, checked_in) all share the same room name but different location_id. A solution that groups by room only will merge them and produce wrong counts.

The trailing-30-day window is not 'all past appointments'. It is status='completed' only and half-open [ep-30, ep). Rows like id 4 (checked_in, 2026-09-04, Exam 1, loc 1) and id 99 (no_show, 2026-09-03, Exam 3, loc 3) fall inside the trailing window for episode 2026-09-30 but must not count in completed_last_30. A wrong status filter or inclusive future boundary will distort them.

Stale future-dated appointments that are already past: id 74 (scheduled, Ear infection re-check, 2026-09-27, Exam 3, loc 2) and id 60 (scheduled, Chronic kidney disease monitoring, 2026-09-27, Exam 1, loc 3) are before episode 2026-09-30 with status 'scheduled'. They must not count in either bucket, but an over-broad 'all scheduled' or 'all future' filter would include them.

Appointments on the episode date itself belong to the future bucket, not the past bucket. For episode 2026-09-30, id 545 (scheduled, Annual check, 2026-09-30, Exam 1, loc 1) is in [ep, ep+14) and counts in booked_next_14; using <= in the past boundary would mis-classify it.

Primary provider tie-break is numeric: if two providers have the same appointment count for a (location, room), choose the lower provider_id. The field is stored as a string but the comparison is numeric.
Idempotency: the agent must delete existing room_turnover and room_turnover_summary rows for this batch (by report + batch_code) before writing; otherwise a rerun would produce duplicate report rows.

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Combines multi-dimensional room turnover (past completed + future booked, distinct patients/providers, primary provider with numeric tie-break) with a cross-location room identity hazard and dual-path SQL vs Python verification. No public benchmark packages this many aggregation concerns into a single report while requiring reconciliation of room name collisions across locations.
